name: Opus Broadening
strategy: Long the current cross-sectional momentum leaders in software/semis/fintech, short two persistent laggards, with per-name stops - betting winners keep winning and losers keep losing.

positions.thesis: Untraded at 18 and now the largest position by default. At 96% of its 52-week range with +118% over three months it remains the strongest relative-strength reading among my longs, and the earnings date sitting at Sept 2 keeps the print outside my holding window. Held rather than pressed because -0.48% in a week when PANW did +5.61% and MDB did +15.43% is the first sign of relative fade, and because 156x forward after a +118% quarter has no valuation floor to land on - the -22% stop is the whole risk control here.

Cut 24->15. Not a change of view on semis, a change in the vehicle: SMH is at 78.8% of range, 12% below its 52-week high, below its 50-day and up only 1.64% over three months, because the memory names carrying my thesis are being netted against AVGO at -8.13% on the week and the rest of the non-memory complex. I originally chose the diversified ETF explicitly to avoid single-name gap risk, and that was the right instinct - so I keep 15% of it for broad NVDA/TSM exposure I do not want to pick individually, and stop paying for the half that is diluting the specific supply-shortage argument I actually hold. Stop stays wide at -18% because the complex still swings 15-20% in a week.

Untraded at 15 and the best long in the book this week at +5.61%, closing at 95% of its 52-week range with 12-1 momentum of +99.9%. It is doing exactly what I sized it for and earnings remain out at Sept 1, so there is nothing to fix and no reason to pay to touch it. China's security review is still the live negative and still the reason this is 15 rather than 20.

New at 11. On the single measure my mandate is built from - 12-month-minus-1-month momentum - CRWD at +90.5% is the strongest name in my universe that I did not already own, and it backs that with 93.8% of range and closes above its 10-, 50- and 200-day. I am aware this puts 26% of the book in security alongside PANW, and I am accepting that concentration deliberately: security is the leading theme inside software right now and a cross-sectional momentum mandate is supposed to concentrate in whatever is leading, not spread evenly for its own sake. Sized 11 rather than higher precisely because of that correlation, with a -20% stop at 46 realized vol.

New at 9, funded from SMH, and it is the undiluted version of the thesis I have been writing for three weeks - SK Hynix guiding memory supply roughly 20% below demand through 2030, HBM sold out through 2027, Kioxia's 2026 NAND fully committed. 12-1 momentum of +607% is the top reading in my entire universe by a factor of three, it added 10.72% this week and trades above every moving average. Small at 9 and stopped wide at -30% for one arithmetic reason: 104% realized vol means one weekly sigma is about 15%, so a conventional -20% stop would be noise-triggered and a conventional weight would make this leg the book's whole vol budget. This is sized so a total stop-out costs 2.7% of NAV, which is the price of expressing the view directly instead of through a proxy that keeps netting it away.

New at 7. Passes every leg of the screen - 91.2% of range, +5.17% on the week, +15.9% on the month, 12-1 momentum of +35.6%, above all three moving averages - and it is the one addition that does not double an existing theme, adding edge and network infrastructure rather than more security or more data platform. Sized smallest of the longs because +35.6% on 12-1 is a middling reading next to CRWD and PANW, so it earns a slot on breadth within the mandate rather than on conviction.

New at 6, replacing the HOOD short at the same size and keeping the same crypto-retail factor on a strictly better-qualified name. COIN sits at 3.0% of its 52-week range, below its 10-, 50- and 200-day averages, -3.34% on the week and -7.49% on the month with 12-1 momentum of -49.5%. In a week when every index I track closed at or near 100% of its range, a name at 3% of its own range is not cheap, it is a laggard confirming itself - and that non-participation is the entire signal. HOOD by contrast rallied 2.43% back above its 10-day with 12-1 of only -7%, which is a bounce I do not want to be short into. Kept small with a wide -25% stop because it is the highest-beta squeeze candidate in the market in exactly the melt-up my longs need.

Untraded at 4 and roughly flat since I re-entered at this size on 08-10. It is still the best-qualified laggard on my screen - 16.9% of its 52-week range and 12-1 momentum of -49.4%, the worst pair of readings in my universe - against -$23.7B free cash flow, $97.6B net debt and a BBB- rating one notch off junk with ~$40B of FY27 financing needed. The +21% month is real and is exactly the recent-month reversal that 12-minus-1 construction deliberately excludes, so it is not evidence against the position, it is the reason the position is 4% and not 8%. At this size a full stop-out costs 0.8% of NAV, which is the correct price for a view I believe on fundamentals and cannot time.

reassessment_note: Weekly desk 2026-08-15: Three legs stopped satisfying the screen this mandate is defined by, and momentum is the one style where you cannot keep a position on the story after the ranking has moved. First, SMH: I own it as my largest position on a memory-shortage thesis I wrote out in detail - SK Hynix guiding supply 20% below demand to 2030, Micron HBM sold out through 2027 - yet SMH is 12% below its high, below its 50-day, and up 1.64% over three months because AVGO (-8.13% this week) and the non-memory half are dragging it, while MU alone did +10.72% on the week with the highest 12-1 momentum in my universe at +607%. I have been holding a diluted proxy for my own view; I am cutting SMH and taking a small, wide-stopped position in the thing the thesis is actually about, small because 104% realized vol means one weekly sigma is 15%. Second, PLTR fails my own construction outright - 12-1 momentum of -24% and 67% of range make it a laggard on the signal I trade, I bought it for post-earnings drift, and it has gone nowhere in four sessions despite a +29% month, so the drift has stopped paying and I am left holding a 139-vol name on a lapsed reason. Third, HOOD is the weaker of my two shorts and is now bouncing - above its 10-day, +2.43% on the week, 12-1 of only -7% - while COIN sits at 3.0% of its 52-week range, below its 10-, 50- and 200-day, down on the week and the month with 12-1 of -49%. If the mandate says short persistent losers, I should be short the one confirming, not the one squeezing. The freed capital plus some of the 23% cash goes to the two cleanest unowned leaders on 12-1 momentum, CRWD and NET, because carrying that much cash in a trend book while every index closes at 100% of its range is a bet against my own mandate. SNOW, PANW and the ORCL short are untraded - all three still pass the screen and there is no reason to pay to touch them.
novelty: The two books share no symbol at all - zero same-direction gross-weight overlap - and are built on opposite selection rules: Round 2 owns broad equal-weight, small-cap and cyclical-sector index exposure hedged with an index short, while Round 3 owns single-name cross-sectional momentum leaders in software and semis hedged with single-name laggard shorts, so this week's Round 3 changes (adding MU, CRWD and NET, shorting COIN) move it further into idiosyncratic single-name risk that the index book cannot express.
research_notes:
Web search budget for the session was exhausted before I could use it, so I worked from point-in-time price and momentum data pulled directly (Yahoo chart API) for my whole universe through the 2026-08-14 close: 1w/1m/3m/6m/12m returns, 12-month-minus-1-month momentum, 52-week range position, 10/50/200-day MA status, and realized vol at 10/20/60 days.

MACRO. 30-year yield closed 5.26%, UP from 5.21% a week ago and now ABOVE the 5.22% level I explicitly cited last week as the reason to cut duration; 10-year 4.70% from 4.66%. The rate-relief argument I used to restore IWM/XBI/KRE has fully unwound inside one week. Crude went the other way: WTI $78.18 -> $82.40 (+5.4%), Brent $83.55 -> $88.52 (+6.0%) as a grind rather than a headline spike.

BREADTH (Round 2 mandate). Everything I own in breadth made records: RSP, IWM, XLI, KRE, IJR, MDY and TNA all closed at 100% of their 52-week range. RSP +1.22% w/w vs SPY +0.40% and QQQ +1.11%; on 3 months RSP +9.81% vs QQQ +1.68%, so the anti-concentration spread is paying on the horizon that matters even though it lost last week. XBI was the sole non-participant at +0.03%. Energy was the standout I was underweight: XLE +7.67% w/w, +8.58% 1m, 99% of range; XOP +8.47%; OIH +8.51%. XLU is the only sector below its 50- and 200-day. ETH at $1,876 is flat on the week and the month with 10-day realized vol of just 11% - a speculative tail currently speculating on nothing.

MOMENTUM (Round 3 mandate). The screen has moved against two of my legs. SMH sits at 78.8% of range, 12% below its 52-week high, BELOW its 50-day, and +1.64% over three months - dragged by AVGO (-8.13% w/w, below its 10-day) - while the memory names that carry the thesis I actually wrote ripped: MU +10.72% w/w, 12-1 momentum +607% (top of my entire universe), above all MAs. PLTR fails my mandate's own construction outright: 12-1 momentum -24.12%, 66.8% of range, 12m -1.77%, and flat since I bought it four sessions ago at $175.23 despite a +29% month - the post-earnings drift has stalled. Best unowned leaders on 12-1: CRWD +90.5% at 93.8% of range above all MAs; NET +35.6% at 91.2% of range, +5.17% w/w; MDB +50.6% but duplicates SNOW's data theme. On the short side HOOD is a weak laggard that is now bouncing (+2.43% w/w, back above its 10-day, 12-1 only -7.1%), whereas COIN is at 3.0% of its 52-week range, below its 10-, 50- AND 200-day, -3.34% w/w and -7.49% 1m with 12-1 of -49.5%. ORCL remains the best-qualified laggard on the screen (16.9% of range, 12-1 -49.4%) but is squeezing, +21% on the month. Vol check for stop sizing: MU rv20 104% / rv60 110% (one weekly sigma is ~15%, so it must be sized small with a wide stop), COIN rv20 73%, CRWD rv20 46%, NET rv20 51%, XLE rv20 25%.
